metadata.summary: A large-scale multiple-choice QA dataset for medical education and entrance examination, containing 194,000 questions spanning 21 medical subjects drawn from Indian medical qualifying examinations (AIIMS/NEET-PG). Each question has four answer options and a single correct answer, covering pre-clinical, para-clinical, and clinical medicine.
metadata.purpose: Benchmarking medical knowledge of language models.
metadata.avoided_uses: Clinical decision support; direct patient-facing applications; inference outside Indian medical curriculum context.

papers.title: MedMCQA: A Large-scale Multi-Subject Multi-Choice Dataset for Medical QA

modality.scope: 21 medical subjects including pre-clinical, para-clinical, and clinical medicine.

ethics.privacy_measures: Data contains no personally identifiable information (PII); derived from publicly released exam materials.
ethics.legal_compliance: Complies with Indian copyright norms for publicly released examination content; no PII or sensitive health data.
ethics.bias_impact_assessment: Explicitly acknowledges India-centric curriculum as a limitation affecting global applicability and equity.

extraction.notes: Baseline card derived solely from dataset_catalog.xlsx real metadata; remaining fields require paper/README or manual completion.
pending_verification: geography.countries is heuristically inferred from limitation text; requires manual verification

known_limitations: Derived from entrance exams (not clinical practice)
Single-correct-answer format does not reflect diagnostic uncertainty
bias_and_limitations.modifications: Questions were reformatted into standardized JSON/CSV; no semantic modification.
bias_sources: Format bias (multiple-choice abstraction from real-world clinical reasoning)
Temporal bias (exam years not specified; possible outdated content)
bias_and_limitations.representativeness_concerns: Over-represents Indian medical education context; underrepresents global clinical practice, diverse patient populations, and non-exam-based knowledge assessment.
bias_and_limitations.long_tail_classes: Subject distribution uneven; some specialties (e.g., community medicine, forensic medicine) have fewer questions.
bias_and_limitations.generalizability_statement: Results may not generalize to non-Indian medical licensing systems or clinical decision-making contexts.
bias_and_limitations.subgroup_coverage: No coverage of demographic subgroups (age, sex, ethnicity) — questions are decontextualized from patient attributes.
bias_and_limitations.missing_data: No patient-level or demographic metadata; no image or multimodal data.

data_origin.selection_rationale: Questions drawn from Indian medical qualifying examinations (AIIMS/NEET-PG) to cover breadth of medical knowledge required for licensure.
data_origin.aggregation_multisource: Aggregated from multiple years and variants of AIIMS and NEET-PG exams.
data_origin.data_shifts_overtime: Curriculum changes across exam years may introduce temporal shifts in topic emphasis or difficulty.

population.target_population: Indian medical students preparing for postgraduate entrance examinations (AIIMS/NEET-PG).
population.inclusion_criteria: Questions appearing in official AIIMS and NEET-PG examinations between unspecified years.
population.exclusion_criteria: Questions not part of official AIIMS/NEET-PG syllabi or formats.
population.missing_groups: Non-Indian medical trainees; practitioners outside India-centric curricula; non-English-speaking learners (all questions in English).
population.subgroups_disparate_outcomes: India-centric curriculum limits generalizability to other national licensing frameworks (e.g., USMLE, PLAB); potential disparities for learners from resource-limited or non-English-medium backgrounds.

annotation.annotation_method: Questions and answers sourced directly from official AIIMS/NEET-PG examinations; correctness verified by domain experts.
annotation.labeling_provenance: Correct answers are official keys from AIIMS/NEET-PG exams.

tasks_and_use.excluded_tasks: Clinical decision support, patient-facing tools, open-ended generation, multimodal reasoning
